parole.significato: abdest (the Islamic act of washing parts of the body using water for ritual prayers and for handling and reading the Qu…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ottoman Turkish آبدست, from Persian آبدست. First attested in 1678.

parole.significato: Turkish child soldier recruited from a conquered country
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish عجمی اوغلان (acemî oğlan, “pupil of Janissaries”). First attested in 1633.

parole.significato: airan
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish آیران (ayran). First attested in 1845.

parole.significato: (historical) akçe (a silver coin minted during the Ottoman Empire, valued at one-third of a para)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ottoman Turkish آقچه. First attested in 1743.

parole.significato: Turkish soldier
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish عسكر (ʿasker), from Arabic عَسْكَر (ʕaskar).

parole.significato: Arabic horse
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish bedawija.

parole.significato: dried fruit and nuts
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بقال, from Arabic بَقَّال (baqqāl).

parole.significato: baksheesh
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بخشش (bahşiş), borrowed from Classical Persian بَخْشِش (baxšiš), from Middle Persian [script needed] (ḤLKWN-šn' /⁠baxšišn⁠⁠/, “bestowal, distribution”).

parole.significato: ensign (the principal flag or banner flown by a ship to indicate nationality)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish [Term?], borrowed from Italian bandiera.

parole.significato: bazaar (marketplace with stalls)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish bazar.

parole.significato: Bey (governor of a province or district in the Turkish dominions)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بك (bey).

parole.significato: binbashi (a major in the Turkish army)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بیكباشی (biñbaşı, literally “leader of a thousand”). First attested in 1821.

parole.significato: Muslim
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish مسلمان (müslimân). First attested in 1612.

parole.significato: mace (heavy fighting club)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بوزطوغان. Compare Bulgarian боздуга́н (bozdugán), Hungarian buzogány, Macedonian боздоган (bozdogan), Romanian buzdugan, and Serbo-Croatian буздован.

parole.significato: scimitar (sword with curved blade)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish, from Persian پولاد, فولاد, from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (pwlʾpt'), 𐫛𐫇𐫓𐫀𐫇𐫅 (pwlʾwd /⁠pōlāwad⁠/).

parole.significato: khan (ruler)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خان (han, “prince, lord”).

parole.significato: stem (narrow part on a tobacco pipe)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چبوق (çibuk, çıbuk, çubuk). The final -ch is due to hypercorrect avoidance of the dialectal -ch > -k change.

parole.significato: Dervish (member of a Sufi Muslim ascetic fraternity of mendicant friars)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish درویش (derviş).

parole.significato: carpet, rug (fabric used as a floor covering)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish دیوان (divan).

parole.significato: djerid (type of throwing spear of Arab origin, usually with a wooden haft and small steel head but sometimes all steel…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish جرید (cirid), from Arabic جَرِيد (jarīd).

parole.significato: emir (title of a prince, commander, or other leader or ruler in an Islamic nation)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish امیر.

parole.significato: a giaour, a non-Muslim, especially a Christian, an infidel; especially as used by Turkish people with particular refere…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish كاور (gāvur), from Classical Persian گَاوُر (gāwur), a variant of گَبْر (gabr, “infidel”); see there for more.

parole.significato: used to speed up the listener's movement or action
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish هایده (hayde), هایدی (haydi).

parole.significato: extortion in the form of protection racket
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خراج (harâc), from خراج (kharāj), from Arabic خَرَاج (ḵarāj).

parole.significato: harem (the private part of an Arab household)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish حرم (harem), from Arabic حَرَم (ḥaram). Doublet of haram.

parole.motivo_incerta: Uncertain; Possibly; modello unc/uncertain; ipotesi scartata nel testo
parole.significato: hubbub, commotion
parole.testo: Uncertain. Possibly borrowed from Ottoman Turkish حرامی + دره (“ravine of the highwayman”), a site of frequent ambushes for Polish envoys heading to Constantinople. Sławski proposes a derivation from Persian غرمیدن (γarmīdan, “to quarrel”), rejected by most scholars.

parole.significato: persimmon (tree)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خرما (hurma), from Classical Persian خُرْمَا (xurmā).

parole.significato: teapot
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ابریق (ibrik, ıbrık), borrowed from Arabic إِبْرِيق (ʔibrīq), possibly borrowed from Classical Syriac ܐܒܪܝܩܐ (ʾaḇrēqā), possibly borrowed from Middle Persian *ābrēk, or possibly borrowed from Parthian *ābrēk.

parole.significato: Janissary, member of Turkish elite infantry
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یڭیچری (yeŋiçeri).

parole.significato: yarligh (khan's written decree)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یرلیغ (yarlık), from Middle Mongol.

parole.significato: yataghan
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یتاغان (yatağan), from Proto-Turkic *jat-.

parole.significato: yogurt (milk-based product stiffened by a bacterium-aided curdling process, and sometimes mixed with fruit or other fla…
parole.testo: Internationalism; compare English yogurt, German Joghurt, Russian йо́гурт (jógurt), ultimately from Ottoman Turkish یوغورت.

parole.significato: saddlebag, kyack
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یوك (yük). Doublet of wiuk.

parole.significato: kaftan (long tunic worn in the Eastern Mediterranean)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish قفتان.

parole.significato: dulce de leche
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish قایماق (kaymak).

parole.significato: caravanserai (roadside inn, usually having a central courtyard where caravans can rest, providing accommodation for tra…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كاروانسَرای, كَروانسَرای.

parole.significato: coffee (beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water)
parole.testo: Internationalism; compare Hungarian kávé, Serbo-Croatian kava, Turkish kahve, ultimately from Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve). Doublet of café.

parole.significato: pouch
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كیسه (kise, kese), from Persian کیسه (kise).

parole.significato: koulan (Equus hemionus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish قولان (kulan, “wild ass”).

parole.significato: clobber (clothing; equipment)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ميدان (meydan).

parole.significato: cloth slipper (slipper with a flexible sole usually made of cloth used as a house slipper)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish مست (mest, “moccasin”). First attested in 1568.

parole.significato: muezzin (person who issues the call to prayer from one of the minarets of a mosque)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish مؤذن (müezzin).

parole.significato: mullah (religious scholar and teacher of sharia law)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ملا (mulla), borrowed from Classical Persian مُلَّا (mullā).

parole.significato: namaz, salat (obligatory prayer that Muslims are called to perform five times a day)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish نماز (namâz).

parole.significato: pilaf
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish پلاو (pilav).

parole.significato: Turkish delight, locoum, rahat lokum (confection made from starch and sugar gel)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish راحت لوقوم.

parole.significato: seraglio (palace)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish سرای (seray, saray), from Persian سرای (sarây).

parole.significato: serdar
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish سردار (serdâr), from Persian سردار (sardâr).

parole.significato: sultan (ruler)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish سلطان (sultān); from Arabic سُلْطَان (sulṭān).

parole.significato: band (strip of material wrapped around things to hold them together)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish طسمه.

parole.significato: bag (flexible container)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish طوربه (torba).

parole.significato: uhlan (lancer, a soldier armed with a lance in a former light cavalry unit of the Polish, Prussian/German, Austrian, an…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish اوغلان (oğlan).

parole.significato: vizier (high-ranking official)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish وزیر (vezir), from Arabic وَزِير (wazīr).
